Purchase Policy
Field Value
Document POL-PUR-001
Version 4.1
Effective 2026-04-01
Owner Purchase department, Northbridge Cycles
Approved by Henrik Weber (plant head)
Status CURRENT
Classification INTERNAL
Version history
Version Date Author Change
1.0 1998-09-01 R. Ainsworth First issue, with the Ledgerline 5 roll-out
2.0 2004-04-01 G. Sutcliffe Rewritten for Ledgerline 6; requests before orders
3.0 2019-04-01 G. Sutcliffe Ledgerline 7.1 migration; direct-order limit £30,000
4.0 2025-04-01 D. Okafor Direct-order limit £50,000; UN 38.3 rule for battery packs and hub motors;
price tolerance 5%
4.1 2026-04-01 D. Okafor §6.2 extended to chargers; §6.4 added; §7.2 price tolerance reduced from 5% to
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.
Internal. Uncontrolled when printed. Page 1 of 4
Northbridge Cycles Ltd POL-PUR-001 | v4.1
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.
Appendix A. Definitions
Term Meaning
Gross value Basic value plus VAT, including freight and packing charged on the order
Lithium-cell part An item with the lithium-cell flag (cell_safety = 1) in the item master
Rate contract An agreed price for a supplier and item for a period, held in Ledgerline
Direct order (DIR) An order without a purchase request, allowed only under §3.3
Internal. Uncontrolled when printed. Page 2 of 4
Northbridge Cycles Ltd POL-PUR-001 | v4.1
Term Meaning
Released (RL) The only status in which the supplier has the order
Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy
When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.
Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.
No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity
requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you
must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.
Does an order require a second approval if the purchase request was already
signed off?
Under section 5.4, the approval given on a purchase request also covers the purchase order raised from
it, so long as the original approver held a limit high enough to cover the gross value of the final order.
If the final gross value has increased beyond that approver's personal limit, a higher-level approval
must be obtained.
What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process
Internal. Uncontrolled when printed. Page 3 of 4
Northbridge Cycles Ltd POL-PUR-001 | v4.1
set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.
What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy
prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If
market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section
7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.
Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?
Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.
Appendix C. Related documents
• POL-SUP-003 Supplier Policy
• POL-APR-002 Approval Matrix for Purchasing
• AMD-PUR-2026-03 Amendment 3 (direct-order limit from 1 December 2026)
• AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy (certificate window)
• SOP-PUR-001 Supplier onboarding
• SOP-PUR-002 Purchase request to purchase order
• MAN-PUR-72 Ledgerline 7.2 User Manual, Purchasing

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 1. Purpose
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 1. Purpose]
chunks.body:
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 3. Requests before orders
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 3. Requests before orders]
chunks.body:
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.

chunks.header:

[Purchase Policy › 3. Requests before orders]
chunks.body: 3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 4. Cost centres and budgets
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 4. Cost centres and budgets]
chunks.body:
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 5. Approval limits
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
chunks.body:
5. Approval limits

5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
chunks.body:
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
chunks.body:
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 7. Prices
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 7. Prices]
chunks.body:
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 8. Tax
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 8. Tax]
chunks.body:
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 9. Records
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 9. Records]
chunks.body:
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.3, § When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › Appendix A. Definitions › Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy › When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?]
chunks.body:
When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.
sections: When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?

well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.

the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, pp.3-4, § Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not y
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › Appendix A. Definitions › Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy › Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?]
chunks.body:
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process
set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.
sections: Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.4, § What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › Appendix A. Definitions › Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy › What rate should I enter on the purchase order?]
chunks.body:
What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy
prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If
market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section
7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.
sections: What rate should I enter on the purchase order?

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.4, § Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an o
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › Appendix A. Definitions › Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy › Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?]
chunks.body:
Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?
Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
sections: Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.4, § At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › Appendix A. Definitions › Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy › At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?]
chunks.body:
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.
sections: At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 1. Purpose
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 1. Purpose]
chunks.body:
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 4. Cost centres and budgets
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 4. Cost centres and budgets]
chunks.body:
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 5. Approval limits
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
chunks.body:
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
chunks.body:
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 7. Prices
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 7. Prices]
chunks.body:
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

[Purchase Policy › 4. Cost centres and budgets]
chunks.body:
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 5. Approval limits
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
chunks.body:
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
chunks.body:
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 7. Prices
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 7. Prices]
chunks.body:
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

chunks.body:
When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.3, § Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
chunks.header:

[Purchase Policy › Appendix A. Definitions › Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy › Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?]
chunks.body:
Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.
No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity
requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you
must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.

chunks.body:
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.

chunks.header:

chunks.body:
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.
Does an order require a second approval if the purchase request was already
signed off?
Under section 5.4, the approval given on a purchase request also covers the purchase order raised from
it, so long as the original approver held a limit high enough to cover the gross value of the final order.
If the final gross value has increased beyond that approver's personal limit, a higher-level approval
must be obtained.
What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.

chunks.header:

chunks.body:
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process
set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.
What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy
prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If
market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section
7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.
Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?
Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.

1. Purpose

pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope

(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.

3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.

centre that will carry the spend.

£50,000 or less.

limit covers the order's gross value.

reference only.

chunks.body:

4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.

chunks.header:

chunks.body:
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.

6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.

5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.

limit covers the order's gross value.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.body:
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 7. Prices
chunks.body:
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.3, § Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
chunks.body:
Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.
No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity
requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you
must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.
sections: Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.3, § How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my
chunks.body:
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.

chunks.header:

chunks.body:
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

chunks.body:
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

reference only.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 1. Purpose
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 1. Purpose]
chunks.body:
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 4. Cost centres and budgets
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 4. Cost centres and budgets]
chunks.body:
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 5. Approval limits
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
chunks.body:
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
chunks.body:
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.

remarks.

8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country

before the supplier is told to deliver.

Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed

including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax

sufficient to cover that gross amount.

well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 1. Purpose
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 1. Purpose]
chunks.body:
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.1, § 4. Cost centres and budgets
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 4. Cost centres and budgets]
chunks.body:
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 5. Approval limits
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
chunks.body:
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.

chunks.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6. Supplier qualification
chunks.header:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
chunks.body:
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

Ledgerline ERP 7.2 Message and Error Code
Reference

Document | MAN-ERR-72

Effective | 2025-01-15
Owner | Ledgerline Systems, Documentation Group
Status | CURRENT
Classification | INTERNAL
1. How to read a message
Every message has a code and a short text in capitals. ERR- codes are errors: the action is refused
and nothing is saved. W- codes are warnings: the action completes, and the warning tells you
something you must act on. The text in brackets, where there is one, is the value that failed the rule.
The second part of the code is the module or area (PO purchase order, SUP supplier, GRN goods
receipt and so on).
2. Codes

units_head.heading: Reference › 1. How to read a message
units_head.text:
1. How to read a message
Every message has a code and a short text in capitals. ERR- codes are errors: the action is refused
and nothing is saved. W- codes are warnings: the action completes, and the warning tells you
something you must act on. The text in brackets, where there is one, is the value
